solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Is murder victim the French mother of Edward III?

parts.note: taken as written
Abel, killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, is the first murder victim
la is the French feminine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether a murdered woman was the French mother of a medieval English king.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella of France, queen of Edward II, bore the future King Edward III.

clue.text: A Scandinavian married in the London area

indicators.note: in places the word for married inside the letters for the London area

parts.note: SE, the south-east, is the region of England around London
to marry is to wed, so married gives wed

explanation.surface: A Nordic person got married somewhere around London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, one of the Scandinavian countries.

clue.text: One becalmed in inlet, Paris banks now close?

indicators.note: in puts one becalmed inside the word for an inlet, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea
one is the indefinite article a
a becalmed boat has been stilled by lack of wind

explanation.surface: A sailor stuck without wind in a small bay, with a separate question about whether Parisian banks are shutting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: on 14 July, the French national holiday, banks in Paris close.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastille Day is France's national holiday, when businesses including banks in Paris shut.

clue.text: "Cryptically ply with it" (Neo, a setting machine)

indicators.note: cryptically tells the solver these words are to be read in a disguised, rearranged way

explanation.surface: A mock quotation from a puzzle-maker telling Neo, from The Matrix, how to work a printing device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptically' rearranges PLY, IT and NEO together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Linotype was a hot-metal typesetting machine that cast whole lines of type.

clue.text: It'll provoke a nervous response on Petticoat Lane I suspect, having no energy

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective meaning dubious or not right, marks these letters as needing to be rearranged
having no means one letter is removed from the pool before rearranging

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone at a London street market says something there will set off a nervous reaction, though they feel drained.
explanation.walkthrough: Petticoat Lane is a famous street market in east London. 'Having no' takes one E out of ONPETTICOATLANEI, and 'suspect' rearranges the remaining fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An action potential is the electrical impulse travelling along a nerve cell when it fires.

clue.text: Mass cleansing unpleasant smell with pumice

parts.note: pumice is a light volcanic rock formed from frothy lava
BO, body odour, is an unpleasant smell

explanation.surface: Scrubbing away a nasty body odour with a pumice stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The lavabo is the priest's ritual washing of hands during the Catholic Mass.

clue.text: Rising medic plundering genuine food store

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards
the medic is plundering by breaking into the word for genuine, so it sits inside it

parts.note: genuine means real
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: An ambitious doctor raids a genuine pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plundering' makes REDRAL; 'Rising' turns that whole word round, as down clues read upwards when reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard where food is kept.

clue.text: Authentication not granted in relation to Roman power

indicators.note: not granted means the authentication document is withheld, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: vis-a-vis means in relation to
a visa is an official endorsement authenticating a traveller's right to enter

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat refuses authentication of something concerning the might of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Vis is the Latin word for force or strength, the power of the Romans' language.

clue.text: Stop anything-but-boring gang going north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means the letters run upwards, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: anything but boring is no drab thing, giving no plus drab
a mob is a gang

explanation.surface: A lively gang heading up north is told to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going north' turns NODRABMOB round as one run. The definition is an organ stop, not a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardon is a deep reed stop on an organ, named after the bass brass instrument.

clue.text: –1 finally scored in maths, perhaps

indicators.note: finally scored means the last letter is scored through, crossed out

parts.note: minus one can be read as less one

explanation.surface: A pupil's score of minus one in a mathematics test.
explanation.walkthrough: Read '–1' as 'less one'; 'finally scored' strikes out its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A maths class is one example of a school lesson, a period of teaching.

clue.text: The way I see it, circumventing anger's boring

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so the anger letters sit inside

parts.note: to me means in my view, the way I see it
ire is anger, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Someone complains that, in their opinion, getting round anger is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and boring are synonyms for something dull and wearying.

clue.text: Not quite the biggest tie writer is wrapping round

indicators.note: round signals the whole assembly is turned about and read backwards
the word is is wrapping the writer, so it goes outside

parts.note: taken as written
the writer of a clue refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A writer wraps a neckband around themself that is nearly the largest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrapping' makes IMES and 'round' turns it backwards. The tie is a sporting fixture, not neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-final is the match just before the final, so a contest one short of the biggest.

clue.text: For consumption, one's found yellowish-brown item on plate

parts.note: consumption is an old name for tuberculosis, TB
one's gives ones, the apostrophe ignored
teak is a yellowish-brown colour, like the wood

explanation.surface: For eating, a person finds a tan-coloured object on their dinner plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumption' looks like eating but is the old name for the disease TB.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone steak is a cut of beef served as a dish on a dinner plate.

clue.text: 19 to move something a distance away

definitions.text: 19 to move something a distance away

parts.words: 19 to move something a distance away
parts.note: 19 refers to the clue answer meaning thought, so this describes thought shifting a distant object

explanation.surface: A description of mental effort used to shift a faraway object.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the supposed power of moving objects by the mind alone, without physical contact.

clue.text: A repeated double-crosser, I shot one of the boys in the money

indicators.note: in places the shot and the boy inside the slang for money

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
a pop is a shot, as in to take a pop at
a lad is one of the boys

explanation.surface: A treacherous gangster confesses to shooting one of the gang over loot.
explanation.walkthrough: A lollipop lady is a British school crossing warden holding a round sign; she crosses the road again and again, hence a repeated double-crosser, not a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A school crossing patrol woman escorts children over the road, back and forth, many times a day.

clue.text: Cockney clockmaker who has ranges within his range?

definitions.text: who has ranges within his range?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial aitch from words

parts.note: a horologist makes or studies clocks

explanation.surface: An East London watchmaker described as having stoves in his stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the London working-class accent known for dropping H. The definition puns on range: mountain ranges within his field of study.
explanation.definitionFit: An orologist studies mountains, so mountain chains fall within his scope of expertise.

clue.text: See 14
I am put off going round the Circle Line?

indicators.note: the put-off word goes round the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: to deter is to put off
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tube passenger is discouraged from riding the Circle line, the loop route on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it means a line through a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is the straight line passing through the centre of a circle from side to side.

clue.text: It's a great idea for anorexic Wenceslas!

definitions.text: It's a great idea for anorexic Wenceslas!

parts.words: It's a great idea for anorexic Wenceslas!
parts.note: the carol king ... King Wenceslas, made skinny, gains the word thin within his title, giving praise for a clever idea

explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is said in praise of a clever suggestion or plan.

clue.text: See 18
Bill's only settle

parts.note: an ad, an advertising bill or poster, the 's read as is
just means only

explanation.surface: An instruction that the only thing to do with a bill is pay it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to settle or arrange something so it fits properly.

clue.text: Mo's tricksily led on by old dear on tour

indicators.note: on tour means travelling around, so the mother goes round the other letters

parts.note: old dear is British slang for one's mother, mum

indicators.note: tricksily means in a tricky way, so these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone called Mo is cunningly strung along by an elderly woman while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricksily' rearranges LEDONBY into OLYBDEN, which goes inside MUM. Mo is the chemical symbol, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Mo is the chemical symbol for this metallic element, number 42.

clue.text: Missing games period, but not with stress

parts.note: missing means having no, giving no
PE, physical education, is the school games lesson

explanation.surface: A pupil skips sports class, though without any anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' means emphasis, not anxiety: the answer is an emphatic negative.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal word is a firmly emphasised no, a negative said with force.

clue.text: Lost through dawn showdown? Half of it

parts.note: per means through or by

indicators.note: half of it takes the first two of the showdown's four letters

parts.note: duels were traditionally fought at dawn

explanation.surface: A defeat in a sunrise confrontation, with only half of it accounted for.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdu is a borrowed French word meaning lost or hidden from sight.

clue.text: The state is rank in a big way

indicators.note: in places the is-rank letters inside the big road

parts.note: the M1 is a major British motorway, read as MI
taken as written
rank means foul or sour

explanation.surface: A claim that a state is offensive on a large scale.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway from London to the north of England; its 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Endlessly look for (and find) bishop's place

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: to seek is to look for and find

explanation.surface: Keep searching until you locate where the bishop lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is his diocese or the seat of his authority.

clue.text: A Jewish month, it's what presumably follows zero-hour

parts.note: 'tis is an old contraction of it is
after hour zero comes hour one, written HR I

explanation.surface: A Jewish calendar month explained as what logically comes after zero-hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tishri is the first month of the Jewish civil year, falling in September or October.

clue.text: Bowled in part of Ashes series, say, in most favourable circumstances

indicators.note: in puts the bowled letter inside the test-match words

parts.note: the Ashes is a series of test matches between England and Australia, so one is a test
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A batsman is bowled during one Ashes cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket test series between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: At best is an idiom meaning under the most favourable conditions or interpretation.

clue.text: Plays tricks — mostly innocent — in the plant

parts.note: to lark about is to play tricks, giving larks

indicators.note: mostly removes the last letter of the word

parts.note: pure means innocent

explanation.surface: Someone plays pranks, almost innocently, in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a flowering plant, a kind of delphinium with spurred blooms.
